I think all of these are harmless. Each name still points at the right element, so the search, the filter and the message box work as they should. Most of the warnings come from two flaws in Koda's own checks; one is a real slip in the app.

## How Koda looks up names
Inside a `ko-item`, an element answers to its `ko-as`, or else to both its `id` and its `name` (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/src/dom/names.js:58-83`). It then warns in two cases (`src/core/names.js:64-73`, reported at `src/dom/refs.js:526-533`):
- **"declared N times"**: the name was added more than once in the item.
- **"is not the #x on the page"**: the page also has an element with that `id`. Koda never checks whether it's the same element.

## Project landing page
`server/views/projects/page.eta:16` wraps the whole page in a `ko-item`. The designs list's `calc-ko-source` and `ko-invoke` (lines 79–80) name `q`, `stageReady` and `stageDesigning`:
- `<input id="q" name="q">` (line 70) gets added twice, once by its id and once by its name. That gives "declared 2 times", but both entries are the same input.
- `q`, `stageReady` and `stageDesigning` are found inside the item, and the page also has `#q`, `#stageReady` and `#stageDesigning`. Those are the same elements, so the "not the #… on the page" warnings are false.

Both are Koda flaws (0.1.4). The app markup is fine.

## Ask for fix page
- **"message" declared 2 times**: this one is real. In `server/views/_composer.eta`, the textarea in `_message-box.eta:7` declares `message` through `ko-as`. The hidden draft input at `_composer.eta:44`, `<input type="hidden" name="message" calc-value="message.value">`, has no `ko-as`, so its `name` declares `message` in the same item too. The textarea comes first, so it wins and the draft still copies the right value. But the clash is genuine.
- **"message" … not the #message**: the textarea has `id="message"`, and the label needs that id. It's the same element, so this is Koda's false positive again.

## The dropped `#app` answer
I agree, you can disregard it. `#app` on the project page (`page.eta:93`) reloads on `event:projects-changed` and `event:app-changed`. One of those events fired just as you clicked "Ask or fix…". The page was replaced before the answer came back, so Koda dropped it rather than attach it to an element that was gone. That's correct behaviour, just reported loudly. It would only be worth looking into if it happened on every visit, which would mean opening the fix page itself triggers one of those events.

## What I'd change
- **`server/views/_composer.eta:44`**: give the hidden draft input its own `ko-as` (e.g. `ko-as="draftMessage"`) so it stops declaring `message`. Leave `calc-value="message.value"` as it is.
- **Koda (`src/dom/names.js` `declarationsIn`, `src/core/names.js` `resolveName`)**:
  - Don't add an element a second time when its `id` and `name` match.
  - Only report "shadows" when the item's element isn't the element with that id.

  This is upstream: the change goes into Koda itself, not this project. Without it, the `q`/`stage*` warnings and the `#message` one will stay. The app could avoid them only by removing `ko-item` or ids that it needs.

1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

text:
There are two separate upgrades here: the Koda that Prelude itself runs on, and the Koda in each project Prelude works on. I'd handle them differently.

## 1. Prelude's own Koda: copy the skills automatically on install
Today, upgrading takes two steps that are easy to forget: `npm install`, then `npm run skills`. `test/skills.test.js` catches the second only when tests run. I'd add a `postinstall` script to `package.json`:

```json
"postinstall": "node tools/copy-skills.js"
```

Then any `npm install` or `npm ci` copies the skills that match the Koda just installed. Upgrading becomes one change to the version in `package.json`, followed by `npm install`. `npm run skills` and the test can stay as a backstop.

This matters more than it looks. `server/main.js:49-53` resolves Prelude's own `@kodalang/core`, and the agent is pointed at its docs and skills (`server/agent.js:392`, `:480`). So every agent session follows whichever Koda Prelude has installed.

## 2. A project's Koda: let Prelude offer the upgrade
Because of that, a project app running Koda 0.1.4 gets an agent following 0.1.5's guidance. When the versions are the same, that's harmless. When they differ, the agent may write attributes the app's Koda doesn't support. Here's what I'd suggest:

- **Spot it.** Read the project's installed `@kodalang/core` version and compare it with Prelude's `kodaVersion`. When the project is behind, show a short notice in the app card on the project page: "This app uses Koda 0.1.4; Prelude knows 0.1.5. Upgrade…"
- **Upgrade on a branch, as a fix.** The button starts a fix, like Ask or fix. Prelude, not the agent (which can't run commands), does the mechanical part in the fix's worktree:
  1. Bump the version.
  2. Run `npm install`.
  3. Copy the skills into the project's `.claude/skills/` if it keeps a copy.
  4. Render every built page.

  The agent's first turn then gets what broke, plus the warnings that changed, and fixes the rest. The person reviews and merges it like any other fix.
- **Point the agent at the right Koda.** When a project has its own `node_modules/@kodalang/core`, have `agent.js` use that copy's docs and skills instead of Prelude's. Fall back to Prelude's only when the project has none.

## How I'd go about it
Part 1 is small and makes no design decisions, so I can do it on its own branch now if you'd like. Part 2 needs a few things the designs don't have yet:
- a design session for the notice and the upgrade flow (Project Landing Page and Fix Something)
- an architecture decision: Prelude would run `npm install` in a project's worktree, which no part does today, and which part does it needs settling

Neither part belongs on this branch, which is only about the warnings. Tell me which you'd like, and whether part 1 should be a separate fix.

Part 1 is done on this branch, but untested: I can't run commands.

## Part 1: what changed
- **`package.json`:** a `postinstall` script runs `tools/copy-skills.js`, so every `npm install` or `npm ci` copies the installed Koda's skills into `.claude/skills/`. To upgrade Koda, you now change its version and run `npm install`. `npm run skills` still works by hand, and `test/skills.test.js` still catches skills that don't match.
- **`tools/copy-skills.js` and `test/skills.test.js`:** their comments say the copy now happens on install.
- **Architecture:** `prelude/prelude-architecture/architecture/parts/tools.md` now lists copying on install among the tools part's jobs. That fits the architecture, so no decision was needed.
- **Fix notes:** I added this to the fix's `NOTES.md`.

**To check:** run `npm install`. It should end with a `copied` line for each Koda skill. Then commit the lockfile, and `.claude/skills/` if it changed, and run `npm test`.

## Prompts for the design sessions
The architecture prompt covers the decision part 2 needs, so I'd run that session first. The other two then build on what it decides.

**Prelude Architecture**
```text
Prelude should help a project upgrade the Koda its app uses. Today the agent always reads the docs and skills of Prelude's own installed Koda (server/main.js resolves @kodalang/core; server/agent.js points the agent at its SKILL.md files and docs/reference.md). A project's app may use a different Koda version, so the agent can follow guidance for a version the app doesn't have.

Propose a decision covering:
1. Which Koda the agent follows. Proposal: the project's own node_modules/@kodalang/core when it has one, and Prelude's only when it has none.
2. Prelude running `npm install` (or the project's package manager) in a fix's worktree. Nothing does that today, and the agent can't run commands. Which part owns it, which parts it may use, and how it stays fenced to the worktree.
3. Where the project's Koda version is read from, and which part compares it with Prelude's version.

Update the parts' files to match, and add a flow for "upgrade a project's Koda" if that helps. Ask me where it's a judgement call, e.g. whether Prelude should upgrade other packages the same way or only Koda.
```

**Project Landing Page**
```text
Add a way to see that the project's app is behind on Koda, and to start upgrading it.

When the app's installed @kodalang/core is older than the version Prelude knows, the project page should say so and offer to upgrade. A starting point: a short line in the app card ("This app uses Koda 0.1.4; Prelude knows 0.1.5.") with an "Upgrade Koda…" action that starts the upgrade as a fix (see the Fix Something design). Follow the Prelude Architecture decision on where the versions come from.

Add states for: up to date (nothing shown), behind, an upgrade already in progress on a branch (link to it instead of offering a second one), and an app with no Koda at all (nothing shown). Keep New design as the page's one primary action. Ask me where it goes and how loud it should be if the app card isn't right.
```

**Fix Something**
```text
Design upgrading a project's Koda as a kind of fix.

The project page starts it ("Upgrade Koda…"). It runs on a branch in its own worktree, like any fix:
1. Prelude, not the agent, changes the version, installs, copies Koda's skills into the project's .claude/skills/ if it keeps a copy, and renders every built page. This follows the Prelude Architecture decision.
2. The agent's first turn is given what changed: the Koda versions, the pages that don't render, and the Koda warnings that appeared or went away. It fixes the app to match, starting with the Koda release notes and docs/reference.md of the new version.
3. The person reviews and merges it as they do any fix.

Design what the person sees: the fix's opening (what's being upgraded, from which version to which), progress while Prelude installs, the case where the install fails (with its output, and a way to try again or give up), and how this fix differs from one the person describes in their own words. Add states for each. Ask me whether the agent should start on its own after the install or wait for me to say go.
```
